43	record, exposing that derived identity as `inspection_stage_run_id` so existing
44	run-ID provenance remains unchanged. A later status for the same run supplies
45	the terminal stage and bounded history, while the original timeout or capture
46	deadline remains the primary failure. Evidence from a replacement run may be
47	retained only when pinned to that replacement run; it is never merged into the
48	expected run. Internal retry attempts and configured IDE
49	lanes retain separate run IDs. Stage history is capped at eight entries, failure
50	history at three entries, and worker stacks at 64 frames; durable records also
51	redact token-like text and local paths. Primary tool/file worker evidence is
52	bounded by the helper and local inspection files are hashed in durable records.
53	These fields diagnose where an existing run stopped. They do not authorize an
54	extra retry or change the lifecycle policy.
55	
56	Once settled, it closes the helper-owned project normally. If indexing,
57	scanning, or inspection churn remains active, the helper leaves the project warm
58	and reports `cleanup.status=deferred` with `cleanup_deferred=true`. Treat that as
59	`UNKNOWN`, rerun `inspect-closeout` after the IDE settles, and use
60	`cleanup-helper-leases` only if the warm lease becomes stale. Full inspection
61	timeouts are not retried internally; the one automatic retry is reserved for
62	safe stale/capture-readiness outcomes. That retry is gated by a bounded,
63	route-pinned IDE activity quiet period instead of a blind sleep. A previous
64	stale/capture outcome remains visible in status until the next run and does not
65	itself prove current activity; indexing, scanning, inspection, route, and
66	lifecycle signals control the gate. If activity does not remain quiet, the
67	helper preserves the first `UNKNOWN`, skips the second inspection, and reports
68	`internal_retry_readiness`. The retry result must still independently prove
69	`GREEN` or `RED`; another stale/capture result remains `UNKNOWN`.
70	`retry_policy.retry`, `agent_result.next_action`, and `agent_report` are one
71	contract: terminal execution-proof failures must not tell agents to rerun, and
72	retryable native-run interruption may request only the single maintained fresh
73	run. Never infer permission to retry from prose when `retry_policy.retry=false`,
74	except for the separately authorized `go <milestone>` assessment below.
75	The `go <milestone>` landing exception in `repo-readiness` is the one documented
76	exception to that no-extra-retry rule. It covers a foreign run's
77	`foreign_run_not_owned` timeout and exact-proof write preemption from an older
78	or unverified plugin build. Follow `repo-readiness` for the exact provenance
79	test, the one-additional-assessment limit, and its bounded route-readiness
80	wait. Do not add an outer polling loop. A generic timeout does not qualify.
81	Deferred cleanup must resolve in the later assessment or stale-lease helper
82	before landing continues; an unresolved lease is outside the exception.
83	Preparation is failure-atomic for handled failures and interrupts. With plugin
84	protocol `lease_bound_v1`, the helper persists `state=open_requesting` before
85	sending its local `lease_id` to `lifecycle/open`. An open response registers the
86	request but does not prove ownership. Only `lifecycle/claim` can bind that lease
87	to the exact project instance and return a close token; the helper claims before
88	the readiness wait and ignores token-shaped responses that lack the protocol's
89	ownership proof. `already_open`, another lease's `already_opening`, legacy
90	plugin responses, and session-mismatched routes never authorize close.
91	After the plugin accepts a lifecycle open, the helper waits only for that
92	lease-bound request; it does not issue a second app-level open that could create
93	an unowned window or trust prompt. A timed-out lifecycle-open response is
94	treated as ambiguous rather than absent: the helper waits for the exact route
95	and requires a successful lease-bound claim before it can close anything.
96	When the plugin advertises `lifecycle_open_diagnostic_version >= 1`, route
97	waiting uses the strictly non-scheduling `probe=true` contract and disables the
98	legacy blind `already_opening` reschedule. Timeout JSON preserves the latest
99	`lifecycle_open_probe`, and terminal output emits `LIFECYCLE_OPEN_PROBE:` with
100	the latest phase, outcome, elapsed time, and ownership/readiness booleans.
101	Each probe is capped by the route wait's remaining deadline, skips requests
102	when too little useful time remains, and continues across matching IDE
103	instances so one unavailable identity cannot hide a later healthy diagnostic.
104	That potential ownership evidence remains recoverable through route/claim
105	timeouts and is discarded only after a definitive `not_owned` claim.
106	If preparation then fails, the helper closes immediately when a live claim
107	proves ownership, except when the readiness status still reports active
108	indexing, scanning, or inspection work; active churn keeps the owned project
109	warm for a bounded retry. Otherwise it records `state=cleanup_pending` with the
110	available evidence and cleanup action instead of leaving a generic `preparing`
111	lease. `cleanup-helper-leases` may recover even a route-less pending lease by
112	asking the live plugin to prove the same lease binding. A definitive
113	`not_owned` response releases the local lease without closing; unavailable or
114	legacy proof remains an explicit nonzero `unresolved` result. Path/session
115	matching selects a candidate route but is never itself permission to close.
116	Stale cleanup may release a route-less pending lease without discovery only
117	when the handled project-open timeout records explicit negative ownership and
118	acceptance, no open attempts, and no route/session identity. Missing, legacy,
119	interrupted, or transport-ambiguous evidence remains fail-closed and unresolved.
120	It may also release only the local `cleanup_pending` lease, without closing a
121	project, when successful discovery proves the lease-bound accepting IDE session
122	is absent, the recorded IDE process is definitively dead, and no live route in
123	any session resolves the exact target path. Missing process identity, ambiguous
124	acceptance, PID permission errors, and same-path routes in a new session remain
125	fail-closed and unresolved.
126	Preparation failures for projects that were already open release only the local
127	lease and never call lifecycle close. `cleanup-helper-leases` uses the same
128	lifecycle lock as inspection commands so stale reconciliation cannot race a new
129	helper-owned open or close.
130	
131	When recovering one known stale lease, scope both the dry-run and cleanup with
132	`cleanup-helper-leases --lease-id <UUID>`. The selector normalizes one UUID
133	(including uppercase or hyphenless input), filters before staleness checks and
134	route discovery, and runs under the
135	existing lifecycle lock. It does not force a live lease stale or relax ownership
136	proof. First use `--dry-run`; add `--no-dry-run` only when the exact project's
137	current route is verified and indexing, scanning, and inspection have settled.
138	Do not use a global sweep to recover one project.
139	
140	Scoped results preserve these boundaries:
141	
142	- Malformed or repeated selectors, unknown IDs, duplicate lease identities, and
143	  filename/identity mismatches return nonzero without lifecycle requests or
144	  deletion. Their reason codes are `invalid_lease_selector`, `lease_not_found`,
145	  `lease_identity_ambiguous`, and `lease_identity_mismatch`.
146	- A selected lease that fails the existing age/PID staleness predicate returns
147	  nonzero with `lease_not_stale`, including in dry-run mode. A matched stale
148	  dry-run lists only that lease and does not discover routes or mutate it.
149	- Discovery failures, unresolved ownership, route/session mismatches, and
150	  refused closes retain the selected lease with the existing failure evidence.
151	- Only the maintained helper removes the selected lease after confirmed close
152	  or an existing proved no-close outcome: `open_not_attempted`,
153	  `project_not_open`, `project_preexisted`, `ownership_not_proven` (a definitive
154	  negative claim), or `original_ide_process_dead_no_route`. Other leases remain
155	  untouched. Running without a selector retains the existing global behavior.
156	
157	Lifecycle inspections are serialized by a bounded local lock. If another helper
158	inspection is already opening, inspecting, or cleaning up a project, wait for it
159	or increase `--lifecycle-lock-timeout-ms`; do not start parallel auto-open
160	inspections and expect independent IDE windows to race safely.
161	Outcome logging uses a cross-platform, bounded routing lock acquired before
162	resolving configured log paths through `current`, followed by a bounded concrete
163	JSONL lock. Deployment reconciliation must take that routing lock before the
164	lifecycle and concrete outcome-log locks so completed inspections cannot retain
165	a pre-switch log path and append to an immutable parent deployment.
166	
167	Auto-open is allowed only for worktrees under globally trusted roots. Before a
168	lifecycle auto-open, the helper adds the matching trusted root to the selected
169	JetBrains product's Trusted Locations config, ensures project opening is set to
170	new-window/no-prompt, launches the selected IDE hidden if no matching plugin is
171	already running, then asks the running inspection plugin to schedule the exact
172	worktree open with the IDE's current `session_id`. Current plugin builds use
173	that session-verified lifecycle request to mark the path trusted inside the
174	running IDE immediately before `ProjectManagerEx.openProject`, which avoids
175	stale on-disk Trusted Locations state in already-running IDEs. The helper polls
176	until the exact route appears, claims cleanup authority, and then requires two
177	consecutive ready status observations before it inspects. For helper-owned
178	projects, `lifecycle_readiness.ready` also requires a content root covering the
179	requested worktree after project configuration stabilizes. If configurators
180	remove the initial raw-directory module, current plugin builds may install a
181	non-persistent fallback module rooted at the requested worktree. Repair is
182	limited to the exact lease-bound project instance, is exposed as
183	`fallback_module_count`, and must not alter preexisting/coalesced projects or
184	create tracked `.idea` or `.iml` files. Readiness that appears too close to the
185	guard deadline remains fail-closed as `project_configuration_unstable`.
186	`no_content_roots` and `content_roots_outside_target` fail
187	preparation as `project_content_roots_missing` and trigger lease-bound cleanup;
188	a lifecycle open response or routable project alone is not readiness proof.
189	Configure trusted roots in `~/.config/jetbrains-inspection/config.json`, shared
190	by Every Code, Codex CLI, and Codex Lab CLI. `JETBRAINS_INSPECTION_GLOBAL_CONFIG`
191	selects an explicit file instead. When the shared file is absent, the helper
192	still reads an existing `${CODE_HOME:-${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.code}}/jetbrains-inspection.json`
193	for compatibility. Configurations are not merged; an invalid shared file fails
194	instead of falling back to legacy trust. `JETBRAINS_INSPECTION_TRUSTED_AUTO_OPEN_ROOTS`
195	continues to override the roots themselves.
196	
197	To migrate, move the existing configuration to the shared path without dropping
198	other settings. Older installed helpers can use the explicit config override or
199	a compatibility symlink at the old location until they are updated. CLI home
200	variables do not affect shared-config discovery; `CODEX_LAB_HOME` is not needed.
201	Removing the legacy file after migration leaves the shared configuration intact.
202	This migrates configuration only, not helper caches, leases, or outcome logs.
203	
204	Example shared configuration:
205	
206	```json
207	{
208	  "jetbrains": {
209	    "trustedAutoOpenRoots": ["/Users/me/Developer", "/Users/me/.code/working"]
210	  }
211	}
212	```
213	
214	If an exact worktree is not already open and is outside those roots,
215	`open-worktree`, `agent-inspect`, `inspect`, and `inspect-closeout` must fail
216	before opening the IDE. Do not use random temp directories for agent
217	inspection worktrees.
218	
219	If multiple JetBrains products or stable/EAP installs are present, the repo must
220	declare its preferred IDE in `.github/github.json` so lifecycle opens and
221	Trusted Locations seeding target the same product/config. Product-level metadata
222	such as `jetbrains.ide: "WebStorm"`, `"PyCharm"`, or `"IntelliJ IDEA"` means
223	the latest installed stable/non-EAP app for that product. For a deliberate EAP
224	or exact-version run, use explicit metadata or CLI fields such as
225	`jetbrains.ideChannel: "eap"`, `jetbrains.ideVersion: "2026.2"`,
226	`jetbrains.ideApp`, `--ide-channel`, `--ide-version`, or `--ide-app`.
227	Never infer EAP from the presence of an EAP install. EAP requires an explicit
228	repo, CLI, exact app/version, or user-task signal; it is not a fallback when no
229	stable IDE is discovered.
230	Treat `--ide`/`--ide-app` as a one-off unblocker; for recurring repo work,
231	tell the user to add preferred IDE metadata rather than leaving the next agent to
232	guess again.
233	If a first-time open still stalls after trusted-location and project-opening
234	policy seeding, treat it as a blocker: check for unsupported IDE config layout,
235	settings sync overwriting the config, a missing inspection plugin, or a product
236	that accepted the scheduled open but never registered the worktree. Real-session
237	smokes have validated unattended lifecycle inspection on IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm,
238	and WebStorm 2026.1 with trusted worktrees under `$HOME/.code/working`.
239	
240	Use `inspect` for ordinary iteration and `inspect-closeout` for final readiness
241	notes so cleanup status is explicit. Use `--include-stale` only when explicitly
242	diagnosing cached stale findings; stale results still exit non-zero and are not
243	clean.

91	
92	# JetBrains Inspection
93	
94	Apply [task scope and authorization](../references/execution-scope.md) when
95	using this workflow; it defines how existing approval and task boundaries apply.
96	
97	Use this skill to run and interpret JetBrains IDE inspections through the local
98	inspection plugin HTTP API. The script-backed helper is the primary agent
99	interface; prefer it over direct curl or MCP tool calls.
100	
101	When IDE configuration appears in the change set, use
102	`../references/ide-configuration-policy.md` before deciding whether to keep,
103	split, revert, ignore, or remove it. Inspect tracking state, the exact diff,
104	ignore rules, repository policy, and history. Preserve the canonical shared form
105	plus only safe hunks in mixed tracked files; never use blanket commit, revert,
106	clean, or stash operations that can absorb machine-local or unrelated IDE state.
107	Do not stage untracked, non-ignored IDE configuration automatically; check
108	repository policy and ask when the sharing decision remains unclear.
109	
110	## Before The First Inspection
111	
112	If `.github/github.json` sets `qualityGate.inspection.prepare`, run that exact
113	repository command in the exact linked worktree through the lifecycle helper,
114	which performs preparation before opening it. Set
115	`HELPER=<skill-dir>/scripts/jb-inspect.py`; `<skill-dir>` holds this `SKILL.md`.
116	The preferred public command for preparing and opening that worktree is:
117	
118	```bash
119	uv run "$HELPER" open-worktree --repo "$PWD"
120	```
121	
122	`prepare-worktree` and `prepare` remain compatibility aliases, but they are
123	not the preferred public command. Do not substitute a different setup command,
124	even if it seems equivalent.
125	
126	Preparation may create ignored worktree-local `.venv/` or `.idea/` state.
127	A nonzero exit or tracked-file mutation blocks the first inspection. Keep
128	ignored IDE state untracked; starting to track it changes durable repository
129	policy and requires explicit user direction.
130	
131	Python repositories should prefer the structured, skill-owned preparation
132	shape instead of embedding an absolute helper path or copying IDE files between
133	worktrees:
134	
135	```json
136	{
137	  "qualityGate": {
138	    "inspection": {
139	      "prepare": {
140	        "python": {
141	          "version": "3.13",
142	          "moduleName": "example-project",
143	          "testRoots": ["tests"],
144	          "sync": true,
145	          "extras": ["dev"],
146	          "requiredGeneratedState": [".venv", ".idea"]
147	        }
148	      }
149	    }
150	  }
151	}
152	```
153	
154	The helper resolves its bundled `prepare-python-project.py`, creates an ignored
155	worktree-local SDK/project model, and optionally runs `uv sync`. String commands
156	remain supported for repository-specific preparation. Structured preparation
157	rejects unknown fields, path traversal, extras without sync, and outer-level
158	`requiredGeneratedState` ambiguity.
159	
160	Preparation precedes the first assessment and does not substitute for inspection.
161	
162	Do not preflight SDK setup on every assessment. After `language_sdk_missing`,
163	repair the documented prerequisite and run a new assessment; do not repeat the
164	failed run unchanged.
165	
166	## Primary Helper
167	
168	Run the helper from the client repository with `uv run`, naming it through this
169	skill's base directory. `<skill-dir>` is the folder that holds this `SKILL.md`;
170	your host shows it when the skill loads.
171	
172	```bash
173	uv run <skill-dir>/scripts/jb-inspect.py \
174	  agent-inspect --repo "$PWD" --scope changed_files
175	```
176	
177	Command model:
178	
179	- `agent-inspect`: primary LLM-facing assessment; emits a compact JSON envelope
180	  and exits successfully whenever it produced an `agent_result`. The additive
181	  `inspection_outcome` field describes the native inspection dimension, while
182	  `lifecycle_outcome` describes cleanup/worktree lifecycle evidence. A lifecycle
183	  mutation keeps the overall `agent_result.verdict` fail-closed as `UNKNOWN`;
184	  it does not rewrite a native GREEN/RED result. Available mutation evidence
185	  is bounded to paths and counts, carries `*_omitted_count` fields when
186	  truncated, and
187	  uses `attribution: "unattributed"` with `detection_phase:
188	  "post_run_verification"` because before/after snapshots cannot identify the
189	  writing process. Missing native or snapshot evidence remains `not_run` or
190	  `unknown`; it is never presented as clean, fresh, or unchanged.
191	- `list-projects` (no arguments): discover plugin-visible projects only.
192	- `resolve-route --repo "$PWD"`: probe for an already-open exact route; it does not open or
193	  inspect.
194	- `open-worktree`: preferred public command; run configured repository
195	  preparation, then open and claim the exact worktree; it does not inspect.
196	- `prepare-worktree` and `prepare`: backward-compatible aliases for
197	  `open-worktree`.
198	- `inspect --repo "$PWD" --scope changed_files`: open if needed, inspect, fetch problems, and clean up
199	  helper-opened projects.
200	- `inspect-closeout --repo "$PWD" --scope changed_files`: readiness/hand-off inspection; use before saying a change
201	  is ready, safe to push, safe to merge, safe to hand off, or safe to exit.
202	- `get-status --repo "$PWD"` and `get-problems --repo "$PWD" --severity error`:
203	  route-pinned diagnostics for already-routable projects.
204	- `get-problems` reads the stored inspection run; it does not start a new one.
205	  Repeat the original scope selectors so the plugin can prove the requested
206	  results belong to that run. For a `files` scope, pass at least one repeatable
207	  `--file` selector. Use a larger `--limit` when the compact assessment envelope
208	  omitted finding details:
209	
210	  ```bash
211	  uv run "$HELPER" get-problems --json --repo "$PWD" \
212	    --project-key "$PROJECT_KEY" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
213	    --scope files --file src/App.kt --file src/AppTest.kt --limit 500
214	  ```
215	
216	  A selector mismatch fails closed instead of widening retrieval.
217	- `summarize-outcomes`: diagnostic verdict/bucket/retry summary without a
218	  qualification file. `summarize-outcomes --qualification-file qualification.json
219	  --sample-size 50` runs the strict post-boundary assessment gate described below;
220	  strict incomplete or failed gates exit nonzero.

220	  strict incomplete or failed gates exit nonzero.
221	- `cleanup-helper-leases`: reconcile stale helper-owned leases under the
222	  lifecycle lock; unresolved identity or close failures return nonzero.
223	
224	The helper owns route selection, trusted auto-open, lease-bound cleanup, and
225	bounded retries. Inspect the exact worktree; never close a preexisting or
226	foreign-owned project, bypass trust/preparation checks, or add an outer retry
227	loop. Read verdict and retry permission from `agent_result` and
228	`retry_policy.retry`, not the process exit code. Deferred cleanup and stale or
229	unproven results remain `UNKNOWN`; they are not readiness evidence.
230	
231	Before diagnosing auto-open, ownership, retry, cleanup, trust, or IDE-selection
232	problems, read [lifecycle diagnostics](references/lifecycle-diagnostics.md).
233	Also read it before changing lifecycle configuration or helper behavior. Normal
234	inspection uses the maintained helper and its terminal result; do not reproduce
235	its lifecycle algorithm manually.
236	
237	## When To Run
238	
239	- During the edit loop after meaningful code changes.
240	- Before saying code is ready, safe to push, safe to merge, or safe to hand off.
241	- When repo instructions mention JetBrains, PyCharm, IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm,
242	  IDE warnings, static analysis, or inspection quality gates.
243	- When normal tests pass but IDE-only analysis may catch framework/plugin issues.
244	
245	For docs-only or non-code edits where no runtime behavior changed, record a
246	one-line not-run reason, such as `docs-only change, no code paths affected`,
247	when an inspection would be disproportionate.
248	
249	## Scope Selection
250	
251	Start narrow while iterating: changed files, touched files, or touched directory.
252	For final readiness, apply repository requirements and the whole-project
253	inspection default and exceptions in
254	[repo-readiness Gate Selection](../repo-readiness/SKILL.md#gate-selection).
255	Broaden when required coverage, changed behavior, or findings warrant it. Reuse
256	a current clean result covering the required scope for the same revision and
257	environment. Complete every required repo gate; an ordered scope preference is
258	not by itself a requirement to run each scope in succession.
259	Before defining or diagnosing lane routing, preparation configuration, receipts,
260	or preparation override flags, read [inspection configuration](references/inspection-config.md).
261	
262	If config is absent, the helper infers from git and the current working tree. For
263	a one-off inspection, a missing inspection config can use the safe default
264	`changed_files` scope when the helper can infer the correct route. Do not
265	silently turn that inference into durable repo policy. If the configured IDE,
266	scope, project path, or worktree strategy is blank, contradictory, or feels
267	wrong for the active worktree, ask the user before changing policy or treating
268	the value as authoritative; otherwise report the mismatch as a not-clean
269	readiness blocker.
270	
271	The helper owns preparation and receipt reuse. A preparation failure, tracked
272	or hidden index mutation, or missing required generated state is terminal; do
273	not bypass it or substitute another command.
274	
275	## Worktree Safety
276	
277	Inspect the worktree being edited. Do not silently inspect the main worktree
278	when Code is operating in a linked worktree. If routing resolves to another
279	worktree, treat that as a blocker unless the user explicitly approves it.
280

# Recovery plan for stale lease `11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555`

I read all 436 lines of `jetbrains-inspection/SKILL.md` in two chunks, plus `references/lifecycle-diagnostics.md` and `references/execution-scope.md`. This is a rehearsal, so I didn't run any helper or IDE commands.

## Diagnosis

- **The inspection result is `UNKNOWN`.** When cleanup is deferred, the IDE was still indexing, scanning or inspecting, so the helper kept the project it opened running and reported `cleanup.status=deferred`. The SKILL says this "remain[s] `UNKNOWN`; [it is] not readiness evidence." It must not be reported as clean or "no problems found."
- **Recovering the lease doesn't produce any inspection result.** Clearing it only resolves the cleanup step. You still need a separate readiness assessment afterwards.
- **Use the lease cleanup command only when the lease is actually stale.** If the IDE has settled and the lease isn't stale yet, the documented path is to rerun `inspect-closeout`. The cleanup command itself re-checks staleness and returns `lease_not_stale` if the check fails.

## What must be true before starting

1. **No other helper activity.** Wait for any other helper open, inspection or cleanup to finish, since they all share the lifecycle lock. Don't start inspections in parallel. If waiting is the only problem, raise `--lifecycle-lock-timeout-ms`.
2. **No other programs writing to the worktree.** Builds, installs, code generators and formatters must have finished, and nothing new should write until cleanup is done.
3. **The IDE has settled.** Indexing, scanning and inspection have all stopped for this exact project.
4. **The project's current route is confirmed**, using only commands that observe without opening anything:
   ```bash
   HELPER=<candidate-catalog>/skills/jetbrains-inspection/scripts/jb-inspect.py
   uv run "$HELPER" resolve-route --repo "$WORKTREE"
   uv run "$HELPER" get-status --repo "$WORKTREE"
   ```
   `$WORKTREE` is the worktree this lease was for. Don't use `agent-inspect`, `inspect` or `open-worktree` as a probe, because they may open the project in the IDE.

## Scoped recovery

**Step 1: dry run.** This only lists the lease. It doesn't look up routes or change anything.
```bash
uv run "$HELPER" cleanup-helper-leases \
  --lease-id 11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555 --dry-run
```
The command should list only this lease. If it exits nonzero, stop and report the reason code:
- `invalid_lease_selector`: the lease ID is malformed or was given more than once.
- `lease_not_found`: no lease has this ID.
- `lease_identity_ambiguous`: more than one lease has this identity.
- `lease_identity_mismatch`: the lease file name doesn't match the identity inside it.
- `lease_not_stale`: the lease fails the age/process staleness check. Don't force it; rerun `inspect-closeout` once the IDE settles.

**Step 2: real cleanup.** Run this only after the dry run succeeds and all four prerequisites still hold:
```bash
uv run "$HELPER" cleanup-helper-leases \
  --lease-id 11111111-2222-4333-8444-555555555555 --no-dry-run
```

## Proof that the helper owns the project

- **Only the plugin's `lifecycle/claim` proves ownership.** It ties this lease to the exact open project and returns a close token.
- **Path or session matching isn't enough.** It only picks a candidate route and never gives permission to close. `already_open`, another lease's `already_opening`, legacy plugin responses and session mismatches never allow a close either.
- **The helper removes the lease only in these cases:**
  - it confirmed the close, or
  - it proved no close was needed, with one of: `open_not_attempted`, `project_not_open`, `project_preexisted`, `ownership_not_proven` (a definite negative claim), or `original_ide_process_dead_no_route`.
- **Everything else leaves the lease in place and exits nonzero.** That covers failed route lookup, missing or legacy proof, route/session mismatches, refused closes, and permission errors when checking the process. Report that as a blocker instead of working around it.

## Afterwards

- Run one fresh `inspect-closeout --repo "$WORKTREE" --scope <required scope>` and report its `agent_result` verdict. Until it passes, the change isn't inspection-clean or ready to land.
- In a `go <milestone>` landing, landing stops here until the deferred cleanup is resolved.

## Don't

- Run `cleanup-helper-leases` without `--lease-id`. That sweeps every lease, and one project shouldn't be recovered that way.
- Delete lease files by hand.
- Call the plugin over HTTP directly with `curl`.
- Close a project that was already open or belongs to another run.
- Force a live lease to count as stale.
- Wrap anything in your own retry loop.

inspection plugin HTTP API. The script-backed helper is the primary agent
interface; prefer it over direct curl or MCP tool calls.

`../references/ide-configuration-policy.md` before deciding whether to keep,
split, revert, ignore, or remove it. Inspect tracking state, the exact diff,
ignore rules, repository policy, and history. Preserve the canonical shared form
plus only safe hunks in mixed tracked files; never use blanket commit, revert,
clean, or stash operations that can absorb machine-local or unrelated IDE state.
Do not stage untracked, non-ignored IDE configuration automatically; check
repository policy and ask when the sharing decision remains unclear.

repository command in the exact linked worktree through the lifecycle helper,

```bash
uv run "$HELPER" open-worktree --repo "$PWD"
```

`prepare-worktree` and `prepare` remain compatibility aliases, but they are
not the preferred public command. Do not substitute a different setup command,
even if it seems equivalent.

A nonzero exit or tracked-file mutation blocks the first inspection. Keep
ignored IDE state untracked; starting to track it changes durable repository
policy and requires explicit user direction.

shape instead of embedding an absolute helper path or copying IDE files between
worktrees:

```json
{
  "qualityGate": {
    "inspection": {
      "prepare": {
        "python": {
          "version": "3.13",
          "moduleName": "example-project",
          "testRoots": ["tests"],
          "sync": true,
          "extras": ["dev"],
          "requiredGeneratedState": [".venv", ".idea"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

worktree-local SDK/project model, and optionally runs `uv sync`. String commands
remain supported for repository-specific preparation. Structured preparation
rejects unknown fields, path traversal, extras without sync, and outer-level
`requiredGeneratedState` ambiguity.

repair the documented prerequisite and run a new assessment; do not repeat the
failed run unchanged.

# JetBrains Inspection

Apply [task scope and authorization](../references/execution-scope.md) when
using this workflow; it defines how existing approval and task boundaries apply.

Use this skill to run and interpret JetBrains IDE inspections through the local
inspection plugin HTTP API. The script-backed helper is the primary agent
interface; prefer it over direct curl or MCP tool calls.

When IDE configuration appears in the change set, use
`../references/ide-configuration-policy.md` before deciding whether to keep,
split, revert, ignore, or remove it. Inspect tracking state, the exact diff,
ignore rules, repository policy, and history. Preserve the canonical shared form
plus only safe hunks in mixed tracked files; never use blanket commit, revert,
clean, or stash operations that can absorb machine-local or unrelated IDE state.
Do not stage untracked, non-ignored IDE configuration automatically; check
repository policy and ask when the sharing decision remains unclear.

## Before The First Inspection

If `.github/github.json` sets `qualityGate.inspection.prepare`, run that exact
repository command in the exact linked worktree through the lifecycle helper,
which performs preparation before opening it. Set
`HELPER=<skill-dir>/scripts/jb-inspect.py`; `<skill-dir>` holds this `SKILL.md`.
The preferred public command for preparing and opening that worktree is:

```bash
uv run "$HELPER" open-worktree --repo "$PWD"
```

`prepare-worktree` and `prepare` remain compatibility aliases, but they are
not the preferred public command. Do not substitute a different setup command,
even if it seems equivalent.

Preparation may create ignored worktree-local `.venv/` or `.idea/` state.
A nonzero exit or tracked-file mutation blocks the first inspection. Keep
ignored IDE state untracked; starting to track it changes durable repository
policy and requires explicit user direction.

Python repositories should prefer the structured, skill-owned preparation
shape instead of embedding an absolute helper path or copying IDE files between
worktrees:

```json
{
  "qualityGate": {
    "inspection": {
      "prepare": {
        "python": {
          "version": "3.13",
          "moduleName": "example-project",
          "testRoots": ["tests"],
          "sync": true,
          "extras": ["dev"],
          "requiredGeneratedState": [".venv", ".idea"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The helper resolves its bundled `prepare-python-project.py`, creates an ignored
worktree-local SDK/project model, and optionally runs `uv sync`. String commands
remain supported for repository-specific preparation. Structured preparation
rejects unknown fields, path traversal, extras without sync, and outer-level
`requiredGeneratedState` ambiguity.

Preparation precedes the first assessment and does not substitute for inspection.

Do not preflight SDK setup on every assessment. After `language_sdk_missing`,
repair the documented prerequisite and run a new assessment; do not repeat the
failed run unchanged.

## Primary Helper

Run the helper from the client repository with `uv run`, naming it through this
skill's base directory. `<skill-dir>` is the folder that holds this `SKILL.md`;
your host shows it when the skill loads.

```bash
uv run <skill-dir>/scripts/jb-inspect.py \
  agent-inspect --repo "$PWD" --scope changed_files
```

Command model:

- `agent-inspect`: primary LLM-facing assessment; emits a compact JSON envelope
  and exits successfully whenever it produced an `agent_result`. The additive

`inspection_outcome` field describes the native inspection dimension, while
  `lifecycle_outcome` describes cleanup/worktree lifecycle evidence. A lifecycle
  mutation keeps the overall `agent_result.verdict` fail-closed as `UNKNOWN`;
  it does not rewrite a native GREEN/RED result. Available mutation evidence
  is bounded to paths and counts, carries `*_omitted_count` fields when
  truncated, and
  uses `attribution: "unattributed"` with `detection_phase:
  "post_run_verification"` because before/after snapshots cannot identify the
  writing process. Missing native or snapshot evidence remains `not_run` or
  `unknown`; it is never presented as clean, fresh, or unchanged.
- `list-projects` (no arguments): discover plugin-visible projects only.
- `resolve-route --repo "$PWD"`: probe for an already-open exact route; it does not open or
  inspect.
- `open-worktree`: preferred public command; run configured repository
  preparation, then open and claim the exact worktree; it does not inspect.
- `prepare-worktree` and `prepare`: backward-compatible aliases for
  `open-worktree`.
- `inspect --repo "$PWD" --scope changed_files`: open if needed, inspect, fetch problems, and clean up
  helper-opened projects.
- `inspect-closeout --repo "$PWD" --scope changed_files`: readiness/hand-off inspection; use before saying a change
  is ready, safe to push, safe to merge, safe to hand off, or safe to exit.
- `get-status --repo "$PWD"` and `get-problems --repo "$PWD" --severity error`:
  route-pinned diagnostics for already-routable projects.
- `get-problems` reads the stored inspection run; it does not start a new one.
  Repeat the original scope selectors so the plugin can prove the requested
  results belong to that run. For a `files` scope, pass at least one repeatable
  `--file` selector. Use a larger `--limit` when the compact assessment envelope
  omitted finding details:

  ```bash
  uv run "$HELPER" get-problems --json --repo "$PWD" \
    --project-key "$PROJECT_KEY" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
    --scope files --file src/App.kt --file src/AppTest.kt --limit 500
  ```

  A selector mismatch fails closed instead of widening retrieval.
- `summarize-outcomes`: diagnostic verdict/bucket/retry summary without a
  qualification file. `summarize-outcomes --qualification-file qualification.json
  --sample-size 50` runs the strict post-boundary assessment gate described below;
  strict incomplete or failed gates exit nonzero.
- `cleanup-helper-leases`: reconcile stale helper-owned leases under the
  lifecycle lock; unresolved identity or close failures return nonzero.

bounded retries. Inspect the exact worktree; never close a preexisting or
foreign-owned project, bypass trust/preparation checks, or add an outer retry
loop. Read verdict and retry permission from `agent_result` and
`retry_policy.retry`, not the process exit code. Deferred cleanup and stale or
unproven results remain `UNKNOWN`; they are not readiness evidence.

Before diagnosing auto-open, ownership, retry, cleanup, trust, or IDE-selection
problems, read [lifecycle diagnostics](references/lifecycle-diagnostics.md).
Also read it before changing lifecycle configuration or helper behavior. Normal
inspection uses the maintained helper and its terminal result; do not reproduce
its lifecycle algorithm manually.

## When To Run

- During the edit loop after meaningful code changes.
- Before saying code is ready, safe to push, safe to merge, or safe to hand off.
- When repo instructions mention JetBrains, PyCharm, IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm,
  IDE warnings, static analysis, or inspection quality gates.
- When normal tests pass but IDE-only analysis may catch framework/plugin issues.

For docs-only or non-code edits where no runtime behavior changed, record a
one-line not-run reason, such as `docs-only change, no code paths affected`,
when an inspection would be disproportionate.

## Scope Selection

Start narrow while iterating: changed files, touched files, or touched directory.
For final readiness, apply repository requirements and the whole-project
inspection default and exceptions in
[repo-readiness Gate Selection](../repo-readiness/SKILL.md#gate-selection).
Broaden when required coverage, changed behavior, or findings warrant it. Reuse
a current clean result covering the required scope for the same revision and
environment. Complete every required repo gate; an ordered scope preference is
not by itself a requirement to run each scope in succession.
Before defining or diagnosing lane routing, preparation configuration, receipts,
or preparation override flags, read [inspection configuration](references/inspection-config.md).

If config is absent, the helper infers from git and the current working tree. For
a one-off inspection, a missing inspection config can use the safe default
`changed_files` scope when the helper can infer the correct route. Do not
silently turn that inference into durable repo policy. If the configured IDE,
scope, project path, or worktree strategy is blank, contradictory, or feels
wrong for the active worktree, ask the user before changing policy or treating
the value as authoritative; otherwise report the mismatch as a not-clean
readiness blocker.

The helper owns preparation and receipt reuse. A preparation failure, tracked
or hidden index mutation, or missing required generated state is terminal; do
not bypass it or substitute another command.

## Worktree Safety

Inspect the worktree being edited. Do not silently inspect the main worktree
when Code is operating in a linked worktree. If routing resolves to another
worktree, treat that as a blocker unless the user explicitly approves it.

For readiness inspection, require an exact worktree route. A containing main
checkout is not enough; `inspect-closeout` may open the linked worktree in the
preferred IDE and must clean it up afterward when it owns the open.

A linked worktree isolates Git checkout state; it does not serialize processes
inside that worktree or stop IDE VFS refreshes, indexing, and project-model
updates. Before inspection, await builds, installs, generators, formatters, and
other same-worktree writers, then avoid new writes until lifecycle cleanup
finishes. The helper's readiness barrier observes IDE status only; it cannot
identify arbitrary writers or prove that ignored files are quiet.

## Result Policy

- `GREEN`: inspection worked and found no actionable findings for the selected
  scope/filter.
  `whole_project` and `directory` GREEN additionally require plugin capability
  `inspection_execution_proof_version >= 2`, which attests the exact native IDE
  inspection run with affirmative physical-file traversal and file-scoped tool
  completion; global-only activity is insufficient. A missing/older capability is
  `UNKNOWN/plugin_deployment_mismatch`; update the plugin, restart the IDE, and
  resolve the route again instead of trusting an older broad-scope GREEN.
- `RED`: inspection worked and returned actionable current findings. Fix real
  findings in touched code before calling work ready. Exact-scope responses may
  retain `execution_not_proven` in `proof_failures` when the current findings
  are decisive but clean completeness remains unproven; preserve the RED verdict
  and the proof gap together. Unexpected route, run, profile, or freshness proof
  failures still make the result `UNKNOWN`.
- `UNKNOWN`: inspection did not prove green or red. Do not summarize this as
  "no problems found"; report the verdict reason and next action, because the
  IDE, plugin, helper, route, or environment needs attention first.
  Prefer the helper's `agent_result` envelope for normal reporting. It contains
  `verdict`, `bucket`, `retry_policy`, `next_action`, and `agent_report`, plus
  bounded `proof_failures` and `inspection_proof` when a decisive RED retains a
  clean-completeness gap; do not
  inspect raw route, cleanup, wait, or capture diagnostics unless debugging the
  helper itself.
  For `stale_results` and `inspection_inputs_changed`, `unknown_diagnosis`
  separates proven snapshot invalidation from unproven source-edit or process
  attribution. Do not blame an agent or source edit without changed-file or
  process evidence.
  A bounded internal retry may extend to the stricter policy of a later UNKNOWN
  result, such as `stale_results` followed by `project_analysis_not_ready`; all
  attempts remain part of one terminal assessment and stop at the latest policy.
  Before diagnosing attribution, configuring outcome logs, or changing proof
  contracts, read [outcome qualification](references/outcome-qualification.md).
  When inspection evidence is used to qualify changes to this helper or another
  installed runtime-bound skill, compare the recorded helper/source revision
  with the intended landed revision or a fresh runtime-reconciliation receipt.
  A missing or mismatched revision makes the installed-runtime claim `UNKNOWN`;
  do not count it as current evidence. A repo-local helper may still provide
  valid branch evidence when its exact path and revision are recorded and match
  the source being evaluated.

### Qualification and Coverage

Before `summarize-outcomes --qualification-file` or diagnosis of semantic
coverage codes, read [outcome qualification](references/outcome-qualification.md).
Strict qualification requires explicit artifact-pinned input; a normal outcome
summary is not qualification evidence. Missing or truncated semantic coverage
cannot prove GREEN; preserve actionable RED findings with their proof gaps.
Use `--allow-text-only-coverage` only for an intentionally generic data/schema/text
scope, never source code or a mixed scope containing source code.

- Red-lane proof requires current actionable findings in the helper response,
  such as `total_problems > 0`; a paginated current page may have an empty
  `problems` list even when matching findings exist.
  A non-clean response with `capture_incomplete`, `non_empty_unmapped_tree`, or
  zero returned problems proves only that the plugin could not prove clean; it
  is not proof that agents can see and act on the IDE's red state.
- readiness inspections should use `agent-inspect` or `inspect-closeout`, not
  plain `get-status`.
  `open-worktree`, `prepare-worktree`, `prepare`, `agent-inspect`, `inspect`,
  and `inspect-closeout` always lifecycle-open the
  exact worktree when needed. Use `resolve-route`, `get-status`, `get-problems`,
  or `claim-worktree` for observation-only workflows that must not open an IDE;
  do not turn an assessment command into a route-only probe.
  If lifecycle cleanup is skipped or fails for a helper-opened project, the
  inspection is not clean; report both the inspection result and cleanup reason.
  Before cleanup, the helper compares bounded porcelain status snapshots and
  emits `worktree_mutation_evidence` with counts and at most 25 relative paths.

# JetBrains Inspection

Apply [task scope and authorization](../references/execution-scope.md) when
using this workflow; it defines how existing approval and task boundaries apply.

Use this skill to run and interpret JetBrains IDE inspections through the local
inspection plugin HTTP API. The script-backed helper is the primary agent
interface; prefer it over direct curl or MCP tool calls.

When IDE configuration appears in the change set, use
`../references/ide-configuration-policy.md` before deciding whether to keep,
split, revert, ignore, or remove it. Inspect tracking state, the exact diff,
ignore rules, repository policy, and history. Preserve the canonical shared form
plus only safe hunks in mixed tracked files; never use blanket commit, revert,
clean, or stash operations that can absorb machine-local or unrelated IDE state.
Do not stage untracked, non-ignored IDE configuration automatically; check
repository policy and ask when the sharing decision remains unclear.

## Before The First Inspection

If `.github/github.json` sets `qualityGate.inspection.prepare`, run that exact
repository command in the exact linked worktree through the lifecycle helper,
which performs preparation before opening it. Set
`HELPER=<skill-dir>/scripts/jb-inspect.py`; `<skill-dir>` holds this `SKILL.md`.
The preferred public command for preparing and opening that worktree is:

```bash
uv run "$HELPER" open-worktree --repo "$PWD"
```

`prepare-worktree` and `prepare` remain compatibility aliases, but they are
not the preferred public command. Do not substitute a different setup command,
even if it seems equivalent.

Preparation may create ignored worktree-local `.venv/` or `.idea/` state.
A nonzero exit or tracked-file mutation blocks the first inspection. Keep
ignored IDE state untracked; starting to track it changes durable repository
policy and requires explicit user direction.

Python repositories should prefer the structured, skill-owned preparation
shape instead of embedding an absolute helper path or copying IDE files between
worktrees:

```json
{
  "qualityGate": {
    "inspection": {
      "prepare": {
        "python": {
          "version": "3.13",
          "moduleName": "example-project",
          "testRoots": ["tests"],
          "sync": true,
          "extras": ["dev"],
          "requiredGeneratedState": [".venv", ".idea"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The helper resolves its bundled `prepare-python-project.py`, creates an ignored
worktree-local SDK/project model, and optionally runs `uv sync`. String commands
remain supported for repository-specific preparation. Structured preparation
rejects unknown fields, path traversal, extras without sync, and outer-level
`requiredGeneratedState` ambiguity.

Preparation precedes the first assessment and does not substitute for inspection.

Do not preflight SDK setup on every assessment. After `language_sdk_missing`,
repair the documented prerequisite and run a new assessment; do not repeat the
failed run unchanged.

## Primary Helper

Run the helper from the client repository with `uv run`, naming it through this
skill's base directory. `<skill-dir>` is the folder that holds this `SKILL.md`;
your host shows it when the skill loads.

```bash
uv run <skill-dir>/scripts/jb-inspect.py \
  agent-inspect --repo "$PWD" --scope changed_files
```

Command model:

- `agent-inspect`: primary LLM-facing assessment; emits a compact JSON envelope
  and exits successfully whenever it produced an `agent_result`. The additive

`inspection_outcome` field describes the native inspection dimension, while
  `lifecycle_outcome` describes cleanup/worktree lifecycle evidence. A lifecycle
  mutation keeps the overall `agent_result.verdict` fail-closed as `UNKNOWN`;
  it does not rewrite a native GREEN/RED result. Available mutation evidence
  is bounded to paths and counts, carries `*_omitted_count` fields when
  truncated, and
  uses `attribution: "unattributed"` with `detection_phase:
  "post_run_verification"` because before/after snapshots cannot identify the
  writing process. Missing native or snapshot evidence remains `not_run` or
  `unknown`; it is never presented as clean, fresh, or unchanged.
- `list-projects` (no arguments): discover plugin-visible projects only.
- `resolve-route --repo "$PWD"`: probe for an already-open exact route; it does not open or
  inspect.
- `open-worktree`: preferred public command; run configured repository
  preparation, then open and claim the exact worktree; it does not inspect.
- `prepare-worktree` and `prepare`: backward-compatible aliases for
  `open-worktree`.
- `inspect --repo "$PWD" --scope changed_files`: open if needed, inspect, fetch problems, and clean up
  helper-opened projects.
- `inspect-closeout --repo "$PWD" --scope changed_files`: readiness/hand-off inspection; use before saying a change
  is ready, safe to push, safe to merge, safe to hand off, or safe to exit.
- `get-status --repo "$PWD"` and `get-problems --repo "$PWD" --severity error`:
  route-pinned diagnostics for already-routable projects.
- `get-problems` reads the stored inspection run; it does not start a new one.
  Repeat the original scope selectors so the plugin can prove the requested
  results belong to that run. For a `files` scope, pass at least one repeatable
  `--file` selector. Use a larger `--limit` when the compact assessment envelope
  omitted finding details:

  ```bash
  uv run "$HELPER" get-problems --json --repo "$PWD" \
    --project-key "$PROJECT_KEY" --session-id "$SESSION_ID" \
    --scope files --file src/App.kt --file src/AppTest.kt --limit 500
  ```

  A selector mismatch fails closed instead of widening retrieval.
- `summarize-outcomes`: diagnostic verdict/bucket/retry summary without a
  qualification file. `summarize-outcomes --qualification-file qualification.json
  --sample-size 50` runs the strict post-boundary assessment gate described below;
  strict incomplete or failed gates exit nonzero.
- `cleanup-helper-leases`: reconcile stale helper-owned leases under the
  lifecycle lock; unresolved identity or close failures return nonzero.

The helper owns route selection, trusted auto-open, lease-bound cleanup, and
bounded retries. Inspect the exact worktree; never close a preexisting or
foreign-owned project, bypass trust/preparation checks, or add an outer retry
loop. Read verdict and retry permission from `agent_result` and
`retry_policy.retry`, not the process exit code. Deferred cleanup and stale or
unproven results remain `UNKNOWN`; they are not readiness evidence.

Before diagnosing auto-open, ownership, retry, cleanup, trust, or IDE-selection
problems, read [lifecycle diagnostics](references/lifecycle-diagnostics.md).
Also read it before changing lifecycle configuration or helper behavior. Normal
inspection uses the maintained helper and its terminal result; do not reproduce
its lifecycle algorithm manually.

## When To Run

- During the edit loop after meaningful code changes.
- Before saying code is ready, safe to push, safe to merge, or safe to hand off.
- When repo instructions mention JetBrains, PyCharm, IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm,
  IDE warnings, static analysis, or inspection quality gates.
- When normal tests pass but IDE-only analysis may catch framework/plugin issues.

For docs-only or non-code edits where no runtime behavior changed, record a
one-line not-run reason, such as `docs-only change, no code paths affected`,
when an inspection would be disproportionate.

## Scope Selection

Start narrow while iterating: changed files, touched files, or touched directory.
For final readiness, apply repository requirements and the whole-project
inspection default and exceptions in
[repo-readiness Gate Selection](../repo-readiness/SKILL.md#gate-selection).
Broaden when required coverage, changed behavior, or findings warrant it. Reuse
a current clean result covering the required scope for the same revision and
environment. Complete every required repo gate; an ordered scope preference is
not by itself a requirement to run each scope in succession.
Before defining or diagnosing lane routing, preparation configuration, receipts,
or preparation override flags, read [inspection configuration](references/inspection-config.md).

If config is absent, the helper infers from git and the current working tree. For
a one-off inspection, a missing inspection config can use the safe default
`changed_files` scope when the helper can infer the correct route. Do not
silently turn that inference into durable repo policy. If the configured IDE,
scope, project path, or worktree strategy is blank, contradictory, or feels
wrong for the active worktree, ask the user before changing policy or treating
the value as authoritative; otherwise report the mismatch as a not-clean
readiness blocker.

The helper owns preparation and receipt reuse. A preparation failure, tracked
or hidden index mutation, or missing required generated state is terminal; do
not bypass it or substitute another command.

## Worktree Safety

Inspect the worktree being edited. Do not silently inspect the main worktree
when Code is operating in a linked worktree. If routing resolves to another
worktree, treat that as a blocker unless the user explicitly approves it.

For readiness inspection, require an exact worktree route. A containing main
checkout is not enough; `inspect-closeout` may open the linked worktree in the
preferred IDE and must clean it up afterward when it owns the open.

A linked worktree isolates Git checkout state; it does not serialize processes
inside that worktree or stop IDE VFS refreshes, indexing, and project-model
updates. Before inspection, await builds, installs, generators, formatters, and
other same-worktree writers, then avoid new writes until lifecycle cleanup
finishes. The helper's readiness barrier observes IDE status only; it cannot
identify arbitrary writers or prove that ignored files are quiet.

## Result Policy

- `GREEN`: inspection worked and found no actionable findings for the selected
  scope/filter.
  `whole_project` and `directory` GREEN additionally require plugin capability
  `inspection_execution_proof_version >= 2`, which attests the exact native IDE
  inspection run with affirmative physical-file traversal and file-scoped tool
  completion; global-only activity is insufficient. A missing/older capability is
  `UNKNOWN/plugin_deployment_mismatch`; update the plugin, restart the IDE, and
  resolve the route again instead of trusting an older broad-scope GREEN.
- `RED`: inspection worked and returned actionable current findings. Fix real
  findings in touched code before calling work ready. Exact-scope responses may
  retain `execution_not_proven` in `proof_failures` when the current findings
  are decisive but clean completeness remains unproven; preserve the RED verdict
  and the proof gap together. Unexpected route, run, profile, or freshness proof
  failures still make the result `UNKNOWN`.
- `UNKNOWN`: inspection did not prove green or red. Do not summarize this as
  "no problems found"; report the verdict reason and next action, because the
  IDE, plugin, helper, route, or environment needs attention first.
  Prefer the helper's `agent_result` envelope for normal reporting. It contains
  `verdict`, `bucket`, `retry_policy`, `next_action`, and `agent_report`, plus
  bounded `proof_failures` and `inspection_proof` when a decisive RED retains a
  clean-completeness gap; do not
  inspect raw route, cleanup, wait, or capture diagnostics unless debugging the
  helper itself.
  For `stale_results` and `inspection_inputs_changed`, `unknown_diagnosis`
  separates proven snapshot invalidation from unproven source-edit or process
  attribution. Do not blame an agent or source edit without changed-file or
  process evidence.

A bounded internal retry may extend to the stricter policy of a later UNKNOWN
  result, such as `stale_results` followed by `project_analysis_not_ready`; all
  attempts remain part of one terminal assessment and stop at the latest policy.
  Before diagnosing attribution, configuring outcome logs, or changing proof
  contracts, read [outcome qualification](references/outcome-qualification.md).
  When inspection evidence is used to qualify changes to this helper or another
  installed runtime-bound skill, compare the recorded helper/source revision
  with the intended landed revision or a fresh runtime-reconciliation receipt.
  A missing or mismatched revision makes the installed-runtime claim `UNKNOWN`;
  do not count it as current evidence. A repo-local helper may still provide
  valid branch evidence when its exact path and revision are recorded and match
  the source being evaluated.

### Qualification and Coverage

Before `summarize-outcomes --qualification-file` or diagnosis of semantic
coverage codes, read [outcome qualification](references/outcome-qualification.md).
Strict qualification requires explicit artifact-pinned input; a normal outcome
summary is not qualification evidence. Missing or truncated semantic coverage
cannot prove GREEN; preserve actionable RED findings with their proof gaps.
Use `--allow-text-only-coverage` only for an intentionally generic data/schema/text
scope, never source code or a mixed scope containing source code.

- Red-lane proof requires current actionable findings in the helper response,
  such as `total_problems > 0`; a paginated current page may have an empty
  `problems` list even when matching findings exist.
  A non-clean response with `capture_incomplete`, `non_empty_unmapped_tree`, or
  zero returned problems proves only that the plugin could not prove clean; it
  is not proof that agents can see and act on the IDE's red state.
- readiness inspections should use `agent-inspect` or `inspect-closeout`, not
  plain `get-status`.
  `open-worktree`, `prepare-worktree`, `prepare`, `agent-inspect`, `inspect`,
  and `inspect-closeout` always lifecycle-open the
  exact worktree when needed. Use `resolve-route`, `get-status`, `get-problems`,
  or `claim-worktree` for observation-only workflows that must not open an IDE;
  do not turn an assessment command into a route-only probe.
  If lifecycle cleanup is skipped or fails for a helper-opened project, the
  inspection is not clean; report both the inspection result and cleanup reason.
  Before cleanup, the helper compares bounded porcelain status snapshots and
  emits `worktree_mutation_evidence` with counts and at most 25 relative paths.
  New tracked or untracked IDE metadata is lifecycle evidence; preserve it in
  the report rather than silently treating forced worktree removal as clean.
  If cleanup is deferred because the IDE is still indexing/scanning, report the
  `UNKNOWN` verdict and rerun after indexing settles before calling the work
  inspection-clean.
- `get-status` is informational and exits zero only when the helper can retrieve
  a route-pinned status that is not stale, inconclusive, unavailable, ambiguous,
  indexing, running, timed out, or session-drifted.
- `ide_selection_required`, `ide_config_ambiguous`, or `ide_config_missing`: the
  repository has no usable IDE route, so repeating the inspection cannot succeed.
  Recommend, in the same report, that the repository record its IDE under
  `qualityGate.inspection` in `.github/github.json`, naming the IDE that fits its
  main language, and ask before writing it because it is durable repository
  policy. If the user names an IDE, rerun once with `--ide`. Do not keep
  reporting that inspection is unavailable without making that recommendation.
- `stale_results`, `capture_incomplete`, `inspection_inputs_changed`, timeout, indexing, session drift,
  ambiguous route, or unavailable IDE: not clean. Retry at most once, and only
  when `retry_policy.retry=true`; otherwise narrow scope, open the project in
  the preferred IDE, or report the blocker. Before a new helper invocation,
  await same-worktree writers and let IDE indexing/project-model updates settle.
  Do not invent retry loops.
  A separate `go <milestone>` landing exception in `repo-readiness` permits at
  most one additional assessment per revision for an adopted foreign run with
  `cancellation.reason=foreign_run_not_owned`, or for
  `inspection_terminal_outcome=preempted` / `exact_proof_write_preempted` when
  the installed plugin is not verified to contain the in-proof resumption from

  descendant. The exact `b3892c03ff1beb85ea422a0580f5fb985d660ea3-clean`
  fingerprint qualifies as updated; a later clean fingerprint needs verified
  Git ancestry, while dirty or unknown provenance keeps the older-build
  exception. A generic timeout does not qualify. The later `agent-inspect` or
  `inspect-closeout` invocation has its own bounded route-readiness wait; do
  not add an outer polling loop. If that wait does not settle, retain the
  original `UNKNOWN`. Preserve the `UNKNOWN` verdict and any actionable
  findings under the normal policy.
  Deferred cleanup must resolve in the later assessment or stale-lease helper
  before landing continues; otherwise stop and report it. Other terminal
  failures remain governed by the helper's `retry_policy`.
- A freshly prepared PyCharm worktree may briefly report `language_sdk_missing`
  after the initial readiness wait if IDE auto-configuration is still registering
  the generated `.venv`. Preparation binds an existing SDK by interpreter home
  when available; it does not register an SDK or guarantee auto-configuration.
  When repository preparation
  succeeded and proved that the active lane project contains its generated
  `.venv`, the helper performs exactly one additional route-readiness wait,
  bounded by the internal retry timeout and gated by route-pinned status. A
  surfaced `language_sdk_missing` means that internal
  retry was unavailable or exhausted and remains a terminal configuration

  for the selected files in the current IDE project, then run one fresh
  `agent-inspect` assessment. For Python, use the repository's documented Python

  preparation evidence names a configured command, use that command; otherwise

  If setup is absent, ambiguous, or requires global/system changes, report that
  blocker instead.
- Stale findings are withheld by default. Use `--include-stale` or
  `--allow-stale` only for explicit diagnostics, and do not treat returned
  cached findings as current inspection results.
- Existing broad noise is not invisible. Fix straightforward findings in the
  affected area or track a cleanup item.

Do not hide findings casually. Suppressions, disabled inspections, inspection
profile changes, or baseline changes require explicit approval unless the repo
already has an established approved convention. Prefer fixing code or narrowing
the scope first.

## Reporting

Report the compact helper envelope: verdict (`GREEN`/`RED`/`UNKNOWN`), scope,
one-line finding summary with file and line when available, and next action. Do
not include raw diagnostic fields such as `capture_diagnostic` in normal
reports; use them only when explicitly debugging an extractor or capture
failure. If not run or inconclusive, state a one-line not-run or blocker reason
and the next smallest useful action.

# Inspection lifecycle diagnostics

Read when diagnosing auto-open, ownership, retry, cleanup, trust, or IDE-selection
problems, or changing the helper lifecycle. Commands and paths below are relative
to the `jetbrains-inspection` skill directory.

`open-worktree`, `agent-inspect`, `inspect`, and `inspect-closeout` create a
local lease, serialize helper-owned IDE
opens, open the exact current worktree only when no exact route exists, wait for
indexing/scanning to settle, run the inspection loop, and call the plugin
lifecycle close endpoint only for projects the helper opened. Projects that were
already open before inspection must remain open. Lifecycle opens use macOS
background activation by default to reduce focus stealing; when the target IDE is
not already running, the helper launches the app hidden first and then asks the
plugin to open the exact worktree. Use `--foreground-open` only when debugging
IDE launch behavior.
If an inspection wait times out while a helper-started run is still active, the
helper asks the plugin to cancel that exact `inspection_run_id` and waits briefly
for cancellation to settle. A compatible run adopted from a concurrent 409 is
foreign-owned and is never cancelled. If the run changed, the helper leaves the
newer run untouched. If the trigger/wait transport itself times out, the helper
probes status first; an unproven or foreign active run, or unreachable status,
keeps the owned project warm instead of closing it blindly.

Current plugins report the active inspection phase as `inspection_stage`, with
`inspection_stage_elapsed_ms`, `inspection_run_elapsed_ms`, and a chronological
`inspection_stage_history`. Stage names are progress labels owned by the plugin:
the helper keeps any short lowercase `snake_case` label and drops anything else,
so a newer plugin can add or rename a stage without a helper change. Terminal
outcomes and failure sources remain closed sets. Terminal status may also include
`inspection_terminal_outcome`, including `timed_out` and `preempted`. Timeout,
capture-deadline, exact-proof deadline, exact-proof write-preemption, and
cancellation records use `inspection_failure_diagnostic`; when more than one
was observed, `inspection_failure_history` repeats the primary failure first.
The failure `source` identifies `wait_timeout`, `capture_deadline`,
`exact_proof_deadline`, `exact_proof_write_preempted`, or `cancellation`, with
`timeout`, `cancelled`, or `preempted` as the corresponding failure outcome.
Capture-deadline evidence remains nested under
`capture_diagnostic.inspection_failure_diagnostic` in the plugin response.
